body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students hear and produce rhyming words (RF.1.2).
- Students identify words in a poem that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses (RL.1.4).
- Students read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate and expression (RF.1.4).

MATERIALS
- The poem Who Sat Where? on chart paper (in the lesson activity)
- Rhyming picture cards: cat/hat, bee/tree, dog/log, sun/bun, cake/lake
- Headphones, so students can listen back to their own Read It Smoothly recordings
- Tablets with the class activities open for recording

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read Poems Are for Saying Out Loud. Read Who Sat Where? aloud with expression. Students clap on each rhyme.
Day 2: Lesson activity: Rhyme Time. Students find the rhyming pairs and make a new rhyme.
Day 3: Echo reading: you read a line, students read it back. Then students record Read It Smoothly.
Day 4: My Rhyme Picture: students draw two things that rhyme and tell about them. Share favorites with the class.
Day 5: Assessment: Poem Reading Check. Each student records a new short poem. Listen for accuracy, smoothness and expression.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: echo read each line before the student records it; it is fine for the first recording to be an echo.
- Support: give rhyming pairs as picture cards and let students pick two instead of thinking of them.
- Stretch: write a new two-line rhyme for the poem and read it to the class with expression.
- Fluency is not speed. Praise smooth phrasing and a voice that matches the poem, never racing.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This week we are reading poems, finding rhymes and practicing reading smoothly. Ask your child to read a short poem or a page of a favorite book to you two or three times. Each time, notice how it gets smoother. Rhyming games in the car help too: what rhymes with cat?
title: Teacher guide: Rhymes and Smooth Reading
